tytul: Lime cordial for the refrigerator (Irish Times recipe)
wstep: This card follows the Irish Times lime cordial by Eunice Power, about 1 litre: lime juice, water, sugar and citric acid, simmered briefly, bottled and kept in the refrigerator.

ostrzezenia.tekst: This is not a tested recipe and the source gives no number of days: University of Wisconsin Extension says untested recipes can be prepared and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, and not on the counter.

akapity: The US FDA list gives limes an approximate pH of 2.00–2.80.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): the source does not measure the acidity of the finished cordial, so do not leave out the citric acid and do not add more water.
Juice of 10 limes, 1 litre of water, 500 g of sugar and 2 teaspoons of citric acid.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): sterilize the bottles as UGA directs for flavored vinegars: wash them in warm, soapy water, then immerse them completely in boiling water for 10 minutes.
Use non-corrodible metal or plastic screw caps, washed in hot soapy water, rinsed and scalded in boiling water.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil.
Add the lime juice and citric acid, stir well and simmer for 1–2 more minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and let the cordial cool.
Pour it into the sterilized bottles, close them and keep them in the refrigerator.
Use the cordial within 2 weeks and do not store it on the counter.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the bottles on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves.
